Add a count column without collapsing rows

Source: R/count.R
add_count.tbl_gpu.Rd

Like count.tbl_gpu(), but keeps every row and column of x and adds the group's count (or weighted sum) as a new column on every row of the group, as dplyr::add_count() does. It runs on the GPU: rows keep their original order, and NA keys form one group, as in dplyr.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
add_count(x, ..., wt = NULL, sort = FALSE, name = NULL, .drop = NULL)

Arguments

x

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Column names or expressions to group by, as count.tbl_gpu(). If x is already grouped, they are added to its grouping for the count; the result keeps x's own grouping.

wt

Optional weight column/expression, as count.tbl_gpu().

sort

If TRUE, sorts the result in descending order of the count column. No rows are collapsed, so every row of a group ties with the others; the sort is stable and keeps their order.

name

The name of the count column. If NULL (default), uses "n", or "nn"/"nnn"/... if "n" already names any column of x (where count.tbl_gpu() and tally.tbl_gpu() look at the grouping columns only), as in dplyr.

.drop

Deprecated in dplyr 1.0.0; supplying it is an error, as in dplyr.

Value

A tbl_gpu with the same rows as x, plus the count column, grouped as x is.

See also

count.tbl_gpu

Examples

library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:cuplyr’:
#> 
#>     bind_cols, bind_rows
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’:
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)
  gpu_mtcars |> add_count(cyl) |> collect()
}
